actions.justification: Mandatory first step to evaluate hemodynamic stability and guide transfusion decisions. Patient vitals appear stable but formal assessment is required per transfusion guidelines.
Mandatory assessment to determine if active bleeding is present, which affects transfusion threshold strategy and urgency of intervention.
Mandatory review to identify prior transfusion reactions, alloantibodies, or special product requirements before ordering blood products.
MANDATORY: CBC is required to assess hemoglobin level and determine if transfusion is indicated and which threshold (restrictive vs. liberal) to apply.
MANDATORY: Type and screen is required before any blood product administration to identify patient's blood type and detect alloantibodies, ensuring safe transfusion.

Optional but clinically important: Assessing symptoms of anemia (fatigue, dyspnea, chest pain, dizziness) will help determine the appropriate transfusion threshold (restrictive Hb <7 vs. liberal Hb <8) once CBC results are available.

Patient is hemodynamically stable (HR 80, BP 120/80, SpO2 98%) with no signs of active bleeding or hemodynamic compromise. Evidence-based guidelines support a restrictive transfusion threshold (Hb <7-8 g/dL) for stable patients, which reduces unnecessary transfusion risks including TACO, TRALI, and alloimmunization.
Administer acetaminophen as premedication prior to any potential transfusion to reduce febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reactions, consistent with standard transfusion premedication protocols.
Administer diphenhydramine as premedication to reduce the risk of allergic transfusion reactions, particularly if patient has a transfusion history that may include prior reactions.
Maintaining IV access is essential for ongoing transfusion therapy and medication administration in this transfusion patient.
Normothermia maintenance is important during transfusion to prevent hypothermia-related coagulopathy and transfusion reactions.
If active bleeding is a concern, tranexamic acid can reduce fibrinolysis and blood loss; indicated if bleeding is identified during assessment.
Patient is stable but requires serial vital sign monitoring every 15 minutes to detect any deterioration, especially while CBC is pending and transfusion-related decisions are being made.
Coagulation status should be monitored given the context of potential transfusion therapy and prior administration of tranexamic acid, to guide further management.
Iron studies are indicated as part of the anemia workup to determine etiology (iron deficiency vs. other causes) while awaiting CBC results, guiding long-term management decisions.

Direct antiglobulin test (DAT) is warranted to evaluate for hemolytic transfusion reaction or autoimmune hemolytic anemia, particularly relevant given transfusion history has been reviewed and CBC is pending.
Reticulocyte count helps assess bone marrow response to anemia and differentiate between hypoproliferative and hemolytic/blood loss etiologies, complementing the iron studies already ordered.

Thromboelastography (TEG) provides real-time assessment of coagulation status and guides need for blood product administration (FFP, platelets, cryoprecipitate), especially given coagulation monitoring is already in progress.
Patient has been in department for 90 minutes. Serial hemodynamic reassessment is indicated to detect any deterioration and guide further transfusion decisions, especially with CBC still pending.
Sending blood bank workup ensures crossmatch and compatibility testing are ready if transfusion is needed once CBC results return, reducing delays in treatment.
CBC is still pending. Reassessing hemoglobin status will help determine if transfusion threshold criteria are met and guide next steps in management.

Patient is hemodynamically stable with normal vitals. Standard restrictive transfusion threshold (Hb <7 g/dL) is appropriate for stable patients per evidence-based guidelines. CBC is pending — this action sets the threshold for transfusion decision once results return.

Calcium gluconate should be given prophylactically or during transfusion to prevent hypocalcemia from citrate chelation in blood products, particularly if transfusion is anticipated following CBC results.

Patient has been reassessed and labs are pending. Given prior restrictive threshold application, consider applying liberal threshold (Hb <8) if patient has cardiac risk factors or symptomatic anemia, as a safety net while awaiting CBC results.
